title: The Lighthouse preflight guard cannot fire, so every PR measures Vercel's login page
description:
lighthouse.yml:162 tests: status 401, OR status 403, OR redirect matching *vercel.com/login*.

Vercel actually answers Deployment Protection with 302 -> https://vercel.com/sso-api?... — so the status is 302, not 401 or 403, and the redirect host path is sso-api, not login. NONE of the three conditions match, the guard passes, and the run proceeds.

Measured on PR #99: it reported performance 0.42, script.size 1354178, third-party.count 4, TBT 1794 — all about vercel.com's login page. Green check, worthless report, and a confident number about a page this project does not own.

This is the eighth catalogued guard-that-cannot-fire in this repository, and the sharpest: it was written specifically to prevent this exact failure, and its own workflow header claims it does.

Two halves to fix: correct the detection (match the real 302/sso-api shape, and prefer asserting the response is OUR page rather than enumerating Vercel's redirect forms — an allowlist of failure shapes is what broke), and set VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET so the job can measure the real preview. The second is the owner's — see gp-dln.281.

title: Turnstile's always-pass test keys cannot produce a successful submission — the Phase 5 gate claims otherwise
description:
Verified against Cloudflare, not inferred: siteverify with the published always-pass secret 1x0000...AA returns {"success":true,"hostname":"example.com"} and NO action field.

src/lib/inquiry/server/turnstile.ts requires action === 'inquiry' and a hostname of ours, so it returns failed -> 400 turnstile_failed. Unsetting the secret fails closed to 503 instead.

So a genuine successful submission is unreachable in ANY environment honouring INV-08.7. That contradicts playwright.config.ts, doc 08 section 5, doc 07 section 5, and the Phase 5 gate's 'form submits on preview'. PR-5.8's unit tests mocked fetch and never met this.

PR-5.10 works around it: the honeypot decoy is the only test reaching the live handler, because doc 07 section 2 answers it at step 3 before siteverify.

Needs a decision — a test seam (env-overridable verify URL, or relaxed action/hostname checks under the published testing secret) or a change to the gate wording. Blocks the Phase 5 gate as written and is a prerequisite for PR-7.2 form go-live.
close_reason: merged in #89. Keyed on exact match against Cloudflare's three published testing secrets, rejecting the env-overridable verify URL because anyone able to set an env var could point verification at a host that always says yes. Safety argument: a testing secret makes siteverify a constant function of the SECRET, not the token, so a deployment holding one already accepts every token and has no protection left to bypass. Production proven unchanged against nine secrets — near-miss, lower-cased, the site key and a real-shaped secret all reject. The e2e workaround routing around the live handler was deleted, which was the real test.

title: The homepage emits no canonical and no hreflang — buildMetadata has no caller
description:
PR-6.8 shipped buildMetadata() and wired it to nothing. On main today:

- src/lib/seo/metadata.ts is the ONLY file mentioning buildMetadata. No caller in src/.
- src/app/[locale]/page.tsx has no generateMetadata at all.
- src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx calls buildRootMetadata, which mentions alternates zero times.

So the site's most important page has neither a canonical nor hreflang alternates, against doc 06 D-06.10 ('every page's alternates.languages carries one entry per enabled locale plus x-default'). The six subpages each call buildMetadata and are correct; only the homepage is not.

This surfaced as a merge blocker on all six subpage PRs. e2e/smoke.spec.ts holds HREFLANG_ALTERNATES_LANDED=false, whose pending half asserts every BUILT route emits ZERO alternates. BUILT is derived from which page.tsx files exist, so the moment the first subpage lands, that route emits 4 and the guard fires — which is exactly what it was written to do.

**The flag cannot simply be flipped.** Flipping it moves the homepage into the asserted half, where it fails for the opposite reason: it emits none. The two fixes are one change and must land together, ahead of PR #60.

title: Apply the zod client fix, then re-set the home-page script budget to what it measures
description:
OWNER DECISION 2026-08-24: do the zod fix, then re-set the number. Motion's eager feature bundle stays as-is — no animation-timing risk taken.

Part 1, the fix (gp-dln.289 has the full measurement): pnpm patch zod, a six-line edit to v4/classic/external.js and v4/core/index.js removing the unshakeable 'export * as locales' and 'export * as core' namespace re-exports. Worth -156,196 raw / -24,865 br on the home route. Pin to zod 4.4.3.

Already measured and REJECTED, do not retry: experimental.optimizePackageImports:['zod'] buys 0 bytes; next/dynamic on InquiryForm is WORSE (+1,362 br) because App Router still SSRs it; zod/mini has the same 'export * as locales'; a leaf-import shim is blocked because zod's exports map does not expose ./v4/classic/*.

Part 2: set the home-page script budget to the post-fix measurement plus a regression margin. Expected around 200,000-215,000 br. The six detail pages already pass 184,320 with 9KB of margin and keep the tighter number.

Expected side effect worth confirming: TBT should come under 200ms. Most of the 272ms is zod INITIALISATION, not download — 52 locale factories and regex tables running during hydration.

title: Retire the simulated LCP gate; measure real users via Speed Insights instead
description:
OWNER DECISION 2026-08-24: measure real users instead of gating on Lighthouse's simulated LCP.

Evidence behind the decision, measured at 15beead: the 2,500ms budget is unreachable on this architecture. Best across every combination tested was 3,930ms. /privacy — the lightest page, no form, no zod — measures 3,533ms while scoring 0.90 performance. The exchange rate is ~5ms LCP per KB of brotli script removed, so closing the last 1,430ms would need ~290KB when the page has 240KB of script total, 130KB of it Next and React. Photography has not landed and will make Load Delay and Load Time non-zero.

Work: drop or de-gate largest-contentful-paint in lighthouserc.cjs, record the reasoning in doc 08 section 7, and wire @vercel/speed-insights field data as the LCP signal. Speed Insights arrives with PR-7.1, so this row either lands with it or lands the de-gating now and the field signal after.
close_reason:
merged in #99. Removed the largest-contentful-paint assertion entirely rather than loosening it — the seat's reasoning: a threshold reset to what the site passes today 'is worse than removing the row, because a number in the assertion table reads as enforcement to everyone downstream of it whatever its severity'. It wrote a standing rule into doc 08 section 7: if a lab LCP assertion ever returns, it must be justified from an observed baseline with a stated regression margin.

Deliberately did NOT wire Speed Insights, for three reasons it named: it is PR-7.1's dependency and that row is blocked on the owner's Vercel setup; doc 10 allows at most one dependency-adding PR open at a time and the zod row is one; and mounting SpeedInsights before the feature is enabled posts vitals to a 404, which is the same defect as the threshold it just removed.

Its twelve-collection evidence is the argument in one shot: LCP 3,466-3,774ms across all twelve, never within 950ms of 2500, while categories:performance medianed 0.91 on the homes — three of four URLs pass the composite containing LCP while every run misses the standalone threshold by about a second, on loopback with no network hop.

title: 84% of LCP is render delay because every revealed block ships at opacity 0
description:
Measured at 15beead with Lighthouse 12.6.1, mobile preset. LCP phases: TTFB 720ms (16%), Load Delay 0, Load Time 0, Render Delay 3,734ms (84%).

The hero is literally <div data-reveal style='opacity:0;transform:translateY(26px)'><h1 id='hero-title'>, so it paints only after hydration. Fonts finish at 212ms, preloaded, display:swap, font-display audit empty. Render-blocking CSS is 14,228 bytes. The only image is the 7,521-byte logo.

Reveal.tsx already supports initial={false}. Forcing all reveals visible moved LCP 4,454 -> 4,125ms on its own.

Note this interacts with INV-05.7 (server HTML byte-identical) and with the no-JS path — a reveal that starts visible is the correct behaviour for a crawler and for prefers-reduced-motion anyway.

title: Zod ships 52 locale files and a JSON-Schema converter to the browser — 156 KB of dead weight
description:
Measured at 15beead. Zod is 261,370 of the home route's 968,559 raw bytes, and only 99,569 of that is validation:

  130,338 bytes — all 52 locale files (he, lt, es, ru, be, fr, hy, pl...)
   31,463 bytes — the JSON-Schema converter (to-json-schema, from-json-schema, processors, generator)

Cause: zod/v4/classic/external.js does 'export * as locales' and 'export * as core', and core/index.js repeats both plus the JSON-Schema exports. Namespace re-exports are not shakeable by Turbopack.

It lands in one home-route-only chunk (320,138 raw / 63,994 br, 86% zod) because InquiryForm is the sole importer and VisitSection puts it on the home page.

MEASURED, not guessed: experimental.optimizePackageImports:['zod'] buys 0 bytes. next/dynamic on InquiryForm makes it WORSE (+1,362 br) because App Router still SSRs it. The only mechanism that works today is pnpm patch zod — a six-line edit to two files, worth -24,865 br on home.

Best bytes-per-risk of anything measured, and it moves three of the four failing budget rows. Risk: a patch file pinned to zod 4.4.3.

title: OQ-08.1 answered with a number: the visual threshold does not catch subtle palette drift
description:

Colour: --color-sage #6f8a5f -> #6f8a72 PASSES. threshold 0.2 is a pixelmatch YIQ budget of ~1409 (35215 x 0.2^2); a 19/255 one-channel shift scores ~20.

So the suite catches layout, type metrics and gross colour, and not subtle palette drift. The seat left the pinned value alone because doc 08 is another row's file. Doc 08 should record the answer, and decide whether a tighter threshold is wanted for the token-bearing shots.

title: Focus after a browser Back has not been built, and after a typed Back it races a wall clock
description:
BackLink handles the two typed navigations; a popstate runs neither, so activeElement stays <body>. PR-6.10 holds this behind a two-position guard (BROWSER_BACK_FOCUS_LANDED) rather than asserting it.

Separately, focusHeadingWhenPresent gives up after 2s and re-mounting the home page can exceed that under load — it failed about half of PR-6.10's local full runs, always on the Back move and never on the forward one. Asserting it would ship a flake D-08.13 forbids, so the transition, the replace, the URL, the hash and the origin heading's existence are asserted and the focus move is not.

Owner: src/components/layout/BackLink.tsx. Both halves are one fix.
close_reason:
merged in #98. Replaced the 2000ms wall clock with BackFocus, a client component in the [locale] layout, mounted on BOTH sides of a navigation that unmounts the page which knows where focus belongs. A useEffect keyed on usePathname cannot run before the commit that changed the pathname — the heading exists by definition, not by budget.

Three parts were wrong first time and each was measured: the popstate listener belongs on BackFocus not BackLink (on BackLink it never fired once — Next's listener registers earlier and React unmounts BackLink inside that dispatch); the origin heading must be markup, because instrumenting proved a fast Back finds the arriving h1 still without the tabindex its mount effect stamps, in 5 of 6 runs; and the pathname guard must read before the request is taken, which was the CI failure.

It also corrected the orchestrator's read of that failure: PER_LOCALE_CASES is routing.locales x FIRST_ROUTE and FIRST_ROUTE is philosophy, so that describe only ever drives philosophy — 'only philosophy fails' was a selection artefact of a matrix the orchestrator had not read, not a signal.

The interesting part: emptying UNLINKED_ROUTE_IDS would have silently killed the Back-half describe, which keyed off the unlinked set — zero tests inside a describe that still looked present. It now keys off a fallback, and a matrix test asserts that fallback produces cases.

title: The 404 is served as an empty streamed shell with no lang and two conflicting robots metas
description:
It renders <html id='__next_error__'> with no lang attribute and no body, then fills on the client. Two <meta name='robots'> tags conflict.

Consequences: a crawler that does not execute JavaScript sees an empty document; a screen reader gets no document language; and the no-JS path (D-07.5) shows nothing at all. PR-6.10's 404 tests use a browser specifically because of this.

Owner: PR-6.1's [...rest] route and not-found.tsx.
close_reason:
merged in #96. Raw bytes before: 22,604 with <html id='__next_error__'>, no lang, an empty body and TWO contradicting robots metas. After: 5,197 bytes, <html lang='en'>, real content, one robots meta — and the same in zh-Hans and zh-Hant, and with JavaScript disabled.

Two findings worth keeping. First, experimental.globalNotFound alone changed NOTHING: Turbopack prefers a root app/not-found.tsx and never bundles global-not-found.tsx while one exists, so the build prints the flag as on while serving the identical shell. Deleting the root file is part of the fix, not cleanup after it.

Second, verified against a pristine 16.3.2 control app: React cannot run an error boundary in the SSR shell, so EVERY notFound() throw yields the recovery document — static, dynamic, or with cacheComponents. Only a URL matching nothing renders whole, which is why the fix routes every unknown path there. A Suspense above the throw turns it into a 200, which INV-06.6 already forbids.

title: An axe exception matched colour pairs unordered, so one allowance excused two defects
description:
Fixed in PR #85, recorded because the CLASS of failure is new here and will recur.

e2e/form-axe.ts's matchException compared the foreground/background pair UNORDERED. The audited entry for the submit button — '#ffffff on #6f8a5f at 3.83:1 — white on sage (the submit button)' — therefore also excused '#6f8a5f on #ffffff' TEXT at the identical ratio: a real AA failure that doc 03 section 10 never passed, silently covered by an allowance written for something else.

The seat found it by deleting the SuccessPanel exception expecting the suite to go red, and watching NOTHING happen. It then oriented the match (axe always reports fgColor as the text colour) and confirmed all four audited entries still match from the run's annotations rather than by inference.

This is the codebase's catalogued 'guard that cannot fail' pattern in a new shape — not a check that never runs, but an EXCEPTION LIST that matches too broadly. Every allowance list in the repo deserves the same question: can this entry excuse something it was not written for?

PR-8.4 lifts these entries to e2e/axe-exceptions.json (D-08.8) and should carry the orientation rule and an expires gate with them.
close_reason: ALREADY-DONE (check-beads-3 @05a65cc). Both halves are fixed: matchException now compares fg/bg in fixed order with a comment explaining the bug, and the sage-on-white AA failure it was hiding was fixed in the same PR (#85). This bead was filed as a pattern record rather than as work, and the pattern is now recorded in the code itself.

title: No a11y check can see inside noscript, and one contrast bug lived there
description:
PR #85 found a third sage link in NoscriptFallback carrying the same LINK_CLASS as the two the axe suite caught. No axe run can reach it: a scripting-enabled browser parses noscript content as text, so it is not in the DOM the checker walks.

That means every accessibility guarantee the site makes stops at the noscript boundary, and the no-JS path is exactly the one a screen-reader user on a locked-down browser is most likely to hit.

PR-8.4 owns the a11y pass. It needs a way to assert on noscript content — parsing the markup directly, or running one pass with JavaScript disabled.

title: Bubble.tsx concatenates caller className onto a real recipe — a latent silent-loss hole

  className={`${display} ${BUBBLE_CARD} ${TAIL_RADIUS[tail]}${className === 
undefined ? '' : ` ${className}`}`}                                         
                                                                            
That is a genuine recipe (flex / hidden lg:flex, flex-col bg-white p-5      
shadow-card-warm-lg md:p-6.5, rounded-bubble-*) with a caller className     
appended raw, so a colliding class loses silently instead of throwing.

a9e21ed (PR #41), after both #30 and #38, so it is a regression the         
migration could not have caught.                                            
                                                                            
Its own doc comment is aware of the hazard — it keeps desktopOnly inside the
recipe 'because display is a property the recipe already sets, and a bare   
hidden from a caller would collide' — and then appends caller classes raw   
anyway.                                                                     
                                                                            
No live defect: the single caller TestimonialsSection.tsx:94 passes lg:mt-  
7.5, a margin the recipe does not set. Latent until the next colliding      
caller.                                                                     
                                                                            
Found by writer-countup-cn while refuting gp-dln.228.                       



PARENT
↑ ○ gp-dln: (EPIC) L3 · Execution plan, index and open questions ● P1

CORRECTION FROM THE IMPLEMENTING SEAT: this is not a silent LOSS, it is a silent COIN FLIP decided by where Tailwind emitted the rule. Measured in chromium at 1280 against the built stylesheet:

  bg-sage, bg-cream, p-0  -> caller LOSES (.bg-sage at byte 28043, .bg-white at 28127)
  hidden, rounded-full    -> caller WINS  (.flex at 15371, .hidden at 15438)

The hidden case is arguably worse than a loss: a caller could silently defeat the onMobile surface flag. withOverrides is right to refuse both directions.

Sweep re-run against today's main confirmed Bubble was the only holdout of 26 className-declaring files; grep for template-interpolated className in src/ now returns nothing. The seat corrected the framing: the bare class is a coin flip on stylesheet emission order, not a loss, and hidden WINS — which could silently defeat the onMobile surface flag.

title: SubpageHeader: a reveal-id collision plus three gaps every detail page works around
description:
**1. Reveal id collision (the one with user-visible consequence).**         
SubpageHeader renders Reveal id=".header", and gallery.header,              
programs.header and menu.header are ALREADY TAKEN by the home sections.

requires for menu.intro. Worked around from outside with an arbitrary child 
selector.

properties ride the table and each section instead of the column.           
                                                                            
Fix in the shell and strip the workarounds from all six pages in the same   
PR. Re-verify in a browser: the spacing changes.                            



PARENT
↑ ○ gp-dln: (EPIC) L3 · Execution plan, index and open questions ● P1

5. SubpageHeader derives intro and introShort independently from message content, so a namespace with introShort but no intro renders with NO intro at all. Dormant today — only philosophy has introShort and it has both — and nothing in the content schema would catch a future violation. Reported by the standing sweep as reasoned, not reproduced.

Findings 2-4 verified as a pure refactor: every element under main#main dumped across all 36 page x width x locale combinations, with the only differences being three intended Menu changes.
